title: Rates Rise
briefing: Case study, inspired by the 2023 failure of a bank that held 'safe' long-dated bonds when interest rates jumped. Two years ago Valtren's treasury put surplus cash into long fixed-rate government bonds for the extra yield.
Rates have since risen two percentage points. Valtren needs cash for a depot expansion in six months. Hollis Varga wants the board paper.

evidence.title: Treasury holding
body: 4,000,000 nominal in 10-year fixed-rate government bonds, bought at par.

evidence.title: Market update
evidence.body: Comparable yields are up 2.0 percentage points since purchase.

evidence.title: Cash plan
evidence.body: Depot expansion: 2,500,000 payable in six months. A 3,000,000 revolving credit line is available at base rate plus 2%.

questions.prompt: Approximately how much value has the bond holding lost? (Enter the loss as a positive figure.)
questions.explanation: Price change is about modified duration x yield change: 8 x 2% = 16% of 4,000,000 = 640,000.

mistakes.feedback: That is 2% of the holding: it ignores duration, which multiplies the effect of a rate change.
Check the units: 2 percentage points is 0.02.

questions.prompt: What is the holding worth now?
How should Valtren fund the depot payment?

options.label: Draw the credit line for the payment and run the bonds down as they mature, then set treasury limits on duration
options.feedback: Avoids crystallising the loss at the worst time and fixes the policy gap that created the mismatch.

options.label: Sell bonds to raise the 2,500,000 now
options.feedback: It works, but it locks in most of the loss on the bonds sold.

options.label: Hold everything and delay the depot
options.feedback: Delaying strategy to protect an accounting position is the wrong way round.

options.label: Buy more bonds now that yields are higher
options.feedback: It deepens the mismatch between long assets and short-term cash needs.

questions.prompt: Which lessons belong in the new treasury policy? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Match the maturity of investments to when the cash will be needed
options.feedback: The mismatch was the real risk.

options.label: 'Safe' assets still carry interest-rate risk
options.feedback: Government bonds have no credit risk but plenty of rate risk.

options.label: Set limits on duration and on how much can be invested long
Never hold any bonds
options.feedback: Bonds are fine within limits; the problem was no limits.

questions.prompt: Rate the liquidity risk from the bond holding as it stands today.
questions.explanation: A forced sale is possible if cash needs grow (possible); a loss of up to 640,000 is moderate for Valtren.

lesson: Interest-rate risk hides in assets labelled safe. Duration times the rate change sizes it; matching maturities to cash needs is the control.
